chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad, from Abdullah ibn Ishaq, from the one who mentioned it, from Muqatil ibn Muqatil, who said:

I asked Abu Al-Hassan (peace be upon him) about the prayer in the beaver and the squirrel, and the fox. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no goodness in all of that except for the squirrel, for it is an animal that does not eat meat'.
ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to pray in the skin of a squirrel according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi illustrates the Shia juristic principle of distinguishing between animals based on their dietary habits to determine the purity of their skins for prayer garments. Imam al-Rida (AS) permits praying in squirrel skin specifically because it is a herbivore, contrasting it with carnivorous animals like the beaver and fox, which are deemed less suitable due to their meat-eating nature. This ruling reflects the broader Shia emphasis on practical criteria for ritual purity rather than rigid categorical exclusions.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Muhammad, from Abdullah Bin Is’haq, from the one who mentioned it, from Muqatil Bin Muqati who said,

‘I asked Abu Al-Hassanasws about the Salāt in the beaver and the squirrel, and the fox. So heasws said: ‘There is no goodness in all that except for the squirrel, for it is an animal not consuming the meat’.
en.sarwar: 16. Ali ibn Muhammad has narrated from ‘Abd Allah ibn Ishaq from those whom he has mentioned from Muqatil ibn Muqatil who has said the following: “I once asked abu al-Hassan, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about performing Salah (prayer) with sable, squirrel and fox. He (the Imam) said, ‘There is nothing good with all of it except squirrel which is an animal that does not eat meat.’”
